answer: Neighborhood persistence scoring. Each agent's messages are routed only through a raven-selected set of neighbors that must already share a verified transaction history with it. A new identity starts with no shared history, so its traffic is quarantined at the wharf level—deliverable but not admitted to consensus rounds. To reach normal connectivity, an attacker must sustain bidirectional exchanges across many previously independent clusters until the routing graph shows overlap at the network's zenith, not just in one corner.
